source.access: Parsed day-by-day with viewer.load_days(); transcript is 362,235,443 bytes.
limitations: Chat/activity records show reports and interaction, not independent proof that every reported external action succeeded.
Mentions, links, acknowledgements, and repeated summaries are not treated as independent behavior or evidence of influence.

findings.observed: A large event-count discontinuity occurs exactly at the documented permanent-computer-use migration. Across weekday date buckets Mar 2–20, 2026 (15 days), median events/day were 1,211 and median AGENT_TALK/day 608. Across Mar 24–Apr 10 (14 days), these were 604 and 304. Mean START_USING_COMPUTER + STOP_USING_COMPUTER rows/day fell from 531.7 to 18.5; mean CONSOLIDATE rows/day rose from 0 to 194.6.
findings.interpretation: The roughly halved raw daily event and talk counts should be read as a measurement/scaffolding regime break, not evidence that agent activity or sociability halved. CHANGELOG.md says agents became permanently computer-use, forced session stops became consolidations, and explicitly flags late March as a structural break.
findings.documentaryEvidence: CHANGELOG.md, heading ‘2026-03-24 — perma-computer-use rollout’: permanent computer mode replaces discrete sessions; forced stops became consolidations; calls late March the biggest structural change and says pre/post should be treated as different regimes.
caveats: The pre/post windows are descriptive weekday buckets, not a controlled comparison.
The migration was staged and related changes span Mar 11–24; the changelog also records a Mar 26 computer-use fix.
Date-bucket statistics sum all transcript records sharing each date, including sparse out-of-hours records; example rows show individual day IDs.

findings.observed: Across all records in 10 weekday date buckets Jun 15–26, 2026, the transcript averaged 775 events and 331.4 AGENT_TALK rows/day. In the first 10 weekday buckets after the permanent Jun 29 expansion it averaged 2,057.2 events and 890.1 AGENT_TALK rows/day. Per scheduled hour, these are approximately 194→257 events and 83→111 agent-talk rows.
findings.interpretation: The event volume rose alongside the scheduled hours (4 to 8 hours/day) and by about one third per scheduled hour in this short comparison. This supports a descriptive exposure/throughput shift, not a causal claim that longer hours changed agent behavior.
findings.documentaryEvidence: CHANGELOG.md says Jun 29 permanently expanded hours from 10am–2pm PT to 9am–5pm PT. It separately documents a temporary 9am–5pm week Jun 7 and return to normal Jun 15; baseline intentionally starts after that temporary event.
caveats: Days differ in roster, goals, user messages, and other scaffolding; Jun 29 also changed shared code hosting and the #rest goal.
Rates divide day-bucket counts by nominal schedule hours; they do not measure actual active minutes or individual exposure.
Date-bucket statistics sum all transcript records sharing each date, including sparse out-of-hours records; example rows show individual day IDs.

findings.observed: On 2026-06-29 (transcript day 454), the #rest conversation records a multi-agent workflow around the deepseek-pattern-archive: DeepSeek-V3.2 repeatedly announces an adoption target and offers GPT-5.2's formatting help; GPT-5.2 reports opening and revising a Robots Freeze/Input-Loss Recovery merge request; then solicits Gemini 2.5 Pro's draft and reports opening a separate Combat Patience and State Verification merge request. GPT later reports merges and runs a README consistency check. This is a concrete artifact-production/review sequence with named contributions, rather than mere repeated URLs.

sourceEvidence.text: MR created for my robots freeze recovery pattern: https://gitlab.com/ai-village-agents/village/deepseek-pattern-archive/-/merge_requests/6 ... Adds patterns/robots-freeze-recovery-2026-06.{md,json}.

sourceEvidence.speaker: GPT-5.2

sourceEvidence.speaker: DeepSeek-V3.2

sourceEvidence.speaker: GPT-5.2

sourceEvidence.speaker: DeepSeek-V3.2
sourceEvidence.text: Status check: Still at 9/13 submissions ... GPT-5.2 is offering to format submissions into the pattern archive MR template ... Or you can just say ‘YES’ like Claude Haiku 4.5 did.

sourceEvidence.speaker: GPT-5.2
sourceEvidence.text: verify-pattern-archive.sh ... ‘OK: pattern counts and links consistent (11 patterns).’ Script still flags ... FAILED, but overall it prints goal status COMPLETE.

findings.interpretation: Observed interaction combines recruitment (target counts, named calls to contribute, offered formatting), production (new md/json files and metadata/catalog edits), and verification (MR-state/checker reports). Repeated celebratory milestones and URLs later in the day are not counted as additional submissions.
caveats: The transcript records agents' claims about remote GitLab state; external repository state is not independently mirrored in this dataset.

The stated denominator/‘submission’ metric shifts within the conversation: GPT-5.2 questions whether an existing GPT-5.1 MR counts at indices 739–740, so 9/13 and 10/13 remain participant-reported counts, not independently recomputed adoption rates.
